meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_180_packages.json, all reference===180 bechina edges from torahData.js, and full source text torah_180.txt. For each statement in the source text, checked whether explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, הַיְנוּ, לְשׁוֹן) is used and whether the concept is captured in the dataset. Concepts connected only by eitza language (עַל יְדֵי, צָרִיךְ, כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ) were excluded from gap consideration.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 4: 'וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַדִּינִין בְּבִינָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: אֲנִי בִינָה, לִי גְּבוּרָה'. This states that the ROOT of judgments is in Binah, connecting it via a proof-verse. The text does NOT say 'דינין הם בחינת בינה' — it states a structural/causal relationship (the root/source is in Binah). This is an eitza connection (judgments are sweetened BY their source in Binah), not a bechina. Excluded per framework.

Lines 4-5: 'יֵשׁ בַּבִּינָה שָׁלֹשׁ יָדַיִם, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם שְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם: יָד הַגְּדוֹלָה וְיָד הַחֲזָקָה, וּכְלָלוּת הַיָּדַיִם הוּא יָד הָרָמָה'. This is a structural description of Binah's inner composition ('there are three hands IN Binah'), not a bechina equating hands to something else. The 'הַיְנוּ' here introduces a specification/breakdown, not a parallel-nature equation. No bechina statement.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: יד הגדולה / יד החזקה / יד הרמה
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The three specific hands are enumerated as components of Binah, not as bechina-equivalents to other concepts in the Torah. They are structural sub-elements used to explain the mechanism of sweetening, introduced with 'יֵשׁ בַּבִּינָה' (there is/are in Binah). This is structural/compositional language, not bechina language. Excluded.

The title 'בְּעִנְיַן סְגֻלַּת הַפִּדְיוֹן' introduces the Torah's topic but the word פדיון is never stated as a bechina of anything. The teaching explains the mechanism of pidyon but does not equate it to another concept with bechina language. Not a gap.
Line 10: 'וְצָרִיךְ לִרְאוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה קַמְצָן, שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר אֶצְלוֹ דִּינִין'. This is a practical warning/instruction (eitza). No bechina statement equating 'miser' to another concept.
Line 10: 'וְלָזֶה צָרִיךְ חָכְמָה יְתֵרָה, לָדַעַת כַּמָּה זֶה צָרִיךְ לִתֵּן'. Extra wisdom is required (eitza — to achieve the goal of not remaining with judgments). Not a bechina.

Lines 6-9: The four worlds are introduced as structural domains in which the three hands operate ('הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה יָדַיִם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל עוֹלָם'). These are contextual/structural references, not bechina-equivalences. No bechina language used.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: שם מב / שם אקיק / שם יקו / שם מה
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Lines 7-9: The divine names are stated as the instruments of sweetening in each world (gematria 42 = 3×יד). These are eitza elements (sweetening is accomplished THROUGH these names), not bechina-equivalences to the core concepts of the package. No bechina language used for the names themselves.
